C1806.title: Unitree UniPwn Humanoid Robot BLE Command Injection Vulnerability (CVE-2025-35027)
C1806.summary: In September 2025, security researchers disclosed a command-injection vulnerability (CVE-2025-35027) in the BLE Wi-Fi provisioning interface of Unitree Go2/B2 quadrupeds and G1/H1 humanoids. All devices shared a hardcoded AES key; encrypting the string "unitree" bypassed authentication, then a malicious Wi-Fi SSID called system() for root. The vulnerability was worm-like — infected robots could auto-scan and infect same-brand robots within Bluetooth range, forming a self-replicating robot botnet. IEEE Spectrum reported UK Nottinghamshire Police were testing an affected Unitree Go2 at the time.
